newsitem.title: USA: Broaddus pleased by improvements in '96 core CPI.
newsitem.headline: Broaddus pleased by improvements in '96 core CPI.

text.p: Richmond Federal Reserve Bank President Alfred Broaddus said Wednesday that while he was pleased with the progress in the core rate of inflation during 1996 it would be shortsighted to dismiss the larger increase in the overall rate.
In remarks to a Wall Street group here and to reporters afterward, Broaddus also said that he was not pleased with recent increases in energy prices.
"I don't want to diminish (the increase in the overall rate) at all," Broaddus told the group.
The Labor Department on Tuesday reported that the consumer price index rose 3.3 percent in 1996 while the core rate, which excludes food and energy, rose only 2.6 percent.
